modify.note: Add an optional title-aware availability method to the calendar service contract.
Implement the optional title-aware availability method for Google.
Implement the optional title-aware availability method for Office365.
Implement the optional title-aware availability method in the telemetry wrapper.
Fall back to ordinary availability when a provider lacks the optional method or title retrieval fails.
Request titles only for overlay mode using the logged-in user's own credentials, with identity checked by user ID rather than username. Keep other availability requests on the ordinary path.
Carry the optional title through busy-time data to the troubleshooter, overlay week view, and conflicting-slot hover card.

Overlay: initialize it with the calendars already selected for conflict checking and fetch their availability immediately after authentication. Use the requested date-range helpers and `lastVisibleDate` input to cover the displayed range. Pass an overlapping event's title through `useCheckOverlapWithOverlay` so the confirmation hover card can show it with the relevant time range. Continue modal: fetch the enabled social-login providers when it opens and offer the corresponding Google or Microsoft action.

Overlay week view shows the busy-time title. Split multi-day and all-day events into day-bounded display segments using `getEventSegmentForDay`, rendering each nonempty segment on its covered day. Keep end-boundary handling consistent so an event ending at midnight does not occupy the following day.
Connect the calendar chosen in the overlay continue modal during the existing sign-in flow and return to the booking page with overlay enabled, without broadening Google OAuth scopes.
